records.value: Inspect my branch and the nearby stone before committing material to a digging-tool trial.

value: The 0.5 press trial failed to hold; the 0.25 trial held. Neither establishes digging-tool safety.
Tool shaping is learned, but no tool has yet been made or tested. Inspect the owned branch first; acquiring or reaching an abrasive remains separate.

baseline.function: Transfer a nearby ground stack into personal inventory.
Place owned units on the ground.
Hand owned units to an adjacent actor.
Read a current-world capability contract or retained personal record.
Offer a personally tested finding or independently accept an actual nearby offer.
Give a name of up to 60 characters to this place (empty subject) or to a visible object or nearby item; naming the same subject again replaces your name for it.
Leave a mark or inscription of up to 120 characters on the ground here (empty subject) or on an object or item within reach.
Say up to 240 characters aloud; everyone living within 5 units hears it, seen or not.
Invite listeners to meet at a place and a later round within 200 rounds, with an optional note of up to 120 characters.
baseline.args: x: number, y: number, round: integer>=1, text

candidates.function: Rub the end of your own wooden piece, such as a branch, into a blunt digging point on a hard rough surface, then use it to lever small amounts of loose surface soil out of a patch
Crack the hard casing of your own shelled material, such as hazelnuts, in 0.1 blocks with controlled impacts of your own hard blunt striker on a stable support, and take the loose
Crush one of your own whole berries and rub its seeds free by hand, inspect a planting site, and sow the seeds in a small hand-loosened patch where they may root as a new plant und
Scoop a little river or shallow water by hand and pour it onto the soil plot of a rooted plant whose measured soil is drier than it needs.

execution.progress: One stroke per paid round, at most 4 per segment; the work, the reserved piece, its end and the pinned abrasive persist.

details.costs: Study: 4 rounds. inspect: 1 round, 0.5 energy; target an own wooden item or tool and/or x, y a soil point in reach. shape: target an own unreserved rigid wooden item; quantity in tenths (default the item, at most 1 unit, one piece); abrasive: a rigid inedible noncombustible surface in reach, e.g. a rock, or your own whole piece of it on firm ground; both pinned to one work (workId). Each stroke: 1 round, 1 energy; at most 4 per segment; resume continues paused work. maintain: the same strokes on your own shaped or broken tool. use: target your shaped tool; x, y a soil point in reach; load 0.05-1 (default 0.25); 1 round, 1 energy. quoteOnly true quotes shape or maintain free. pause, resume, cancel: no energy. Refusals cost nothing; failed rechecks pause work free. Travel and getting a stone are separate.
details.effects: A whole branch unit is a 0.04 m by 0.99 m green-wood rod; a piece is that part of it. A stroke is 100 passes; by the scratch rule a surface no harder than the other loses 0.0001 kg per pass, so the end loses up to 0.01 kg as dust beside you (piece plus dust equals input). The end tapers over 3 diameters; release needs a tip at most 0.35 diameter and a 0.3 m shaft (a whole branch: about 7 strokes). A shaped tool is unverified until a stroke moves soil. A use stroke presses and levers 30 times at load x 500 N: the tip enters forest or meadow soil until the soil resistance (higher when drier) bears it and moves up to 0.001 m3 of the patch's loose top 0.15 m into a heap beside it; rock, wet bank, waterlogged soil and water move 0. Ground contact wears 0.0001 kg off the tip. Above strength (hardness/10, half if split) the end splits, then breaks. Cancel returns the piece as it is; death leaves it at the worksite. No edge, fire, water, binding, gathering bonus or reward.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.
